feedback: This candidate continues the established trend of tuning the PID controller to reduce steering oscillations and improve stability, following the rationale and feedback from iteration 2. The proportional gain kp is increased slightly from 2 to 3 to improve responsiveness and avoid sluggishness, while the derivative gain kd is decreased slightly from 10 to 9 to balance damping and responsiveness. The base speed is reduced from 1.7 to 1.6 to balance speed and control stability, addressing the risk of instability or low progress at higher speeds. The integral gain ki remains at 0.5, maintaining integral action, and sensor weights and line loss strategy remain unchanged, as no issues have been reported with them. The geometry is unchanged, preserving a stable physical setup. Depending on the next race results, if steering oscillations persist despite these adjustments, consider further fine-tuning kd and kp; if progress is low or unstable, adjust base speed accordingly; if line loss events occur, consider revising sensor weights or line loss strategy. Overall, this candidate is a reasonable refinement based on prior evidence and worth racing to gather concrete performance data.
